blocks.text: The Guru’s reasoning turns explicitly toward the poor and marginalized communities: power should not be handed to those already enthroned, but to the neglected people whom the house of Nanak had always sheltered. (18–19)

The passage lists peasants, artisans, laborers, service castes, traders, and other socially disregarded groups as the ones who would receive dignity, brotherhood, and a claim to sovereignty through the Guru’s favor. (20–22)

When Guru Gobind Singh calls such followers to take up arms against the Mughals, many shrink back in fear before imperial power, still imagining themselves as sparrows and lambs before hawks and lions. (23–25)
